title: Calculation methods - Introduction
heading: Calculation methods
start_phrase: Calculation methods for calculating Swedbank’s total emissions in scopes 1–3 are presented below.
summary: Introduces Swedbank’s annual greenhouse gas accounting methodology using the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline), with access and quality control (input data, market-based energy certificates, calculations) by U&We, aligned to the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard. Emissions are quantified as CO2e with GWPs for all seven Kyoto gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, NF3, SF6, PFCs). Scope 1 covers direct emissions from stationary fuels, company-owned vehicles (estimated via financial controls), and refrigerant leakage (operational controls based on refrigerant type/weight). Scope 2 covers purchased electricity, heating, and steam, calculated using both location-based and market-based methods with supplier-specific factors; contractual instruments (energy attribute certificates, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights) covered 37% of 2024 consumption, were quality-checked by U&We, and residual factors were applied where instruments failed criteria or were absent; boundary is operations where Swedbank has operational control (branches/buildings). Scope 3 includes business travel, security transports, paper, water, waste, manufacturing of employees’ IT equipment, and financed emissions from the lending portfolio and Swedbank Robur Fonder; methods support tracking of climate targets referenced in section E1-4.
text:
Calculation methods 
1) Swedbank annually conducts a calculation using the Our Impacts platform, provided by the software developer EcoOnline. Access to the platform is managed by U&We, which also performs 
 quality control of input data, market-based energy certificates, and calculations. The calculation is conducted in accordance with the World Business Council for Sustainable Development and 
World Resources Institute’s (WBCSD/WRI) Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard. The emission calculation in the Our Impacts platform 
 quantifies all seven Kyoto greenhouse gases where applicable, and measures them in units of carbon dioxide equivalents, CO2e. The seven gases are carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), 
nitrous oxide (N2O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), nitrogen trifluoride (NF3), sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), and perfluorocarbons (PFCs). The global warming potential (GWP) for each gas is applied.Calculation methods for calculating Swedbank’s total emissions in scopes 1–3 
are presented below. The methodology for calculating emissions is based on 
the GHG protocol. These methods are also used to be able to follow up on the 
set  climate targets that are presented under section E1-4. Below are descriptions 
for each scope:
• Scope 1 includes direct greenhouse gas emissions from sources owned or 
controlled by the company, such as stationary fuels for energy and heating, 
company-owned vehicles and refrigerant leakage. Emissions from Swed -
bank’s company-owned vehicles are estimated on the basis of the Group’s financial controls. Emissions from Swedbank’s cooling systems are calcu -
lated using operational controls (based on weight and type of refrigerant used in the cooling system).
• Scope 2 includes greenhouse gas emissions from the generation of pur-
chased electricity, heating and steam generated outside operations. Given that 
Swedbank operates in European electricity markets that offer market-based 
contractual instruments, supplier-specific emission factors are taken into 
account when calculating scope 2. Scope 2 emissions are calculated using 
both a location-based an a market-based method. The location-based method 
applies average emission factors corresponding to the grid where consump-
tion takes place, while the market-based method applies emission factors 
 corresponding to energy purchased (or not purchased) through contractual 
instruments. Contractual instruments include energy attribute certificates, direct energy contracts, PPAs and supplier-specific emission rights. Contrac -
tual instruments represented 37% of total consumption in 2024. In the calcula-tion, U&We assessed whether the contractual instruments presented met the 
established quality criteria. Where contractual instruments did not meet the 
quality criteria, or where contractual instruments were not purchased, market  -
based scope 2 emissions were calculated using residual factors. Scope 2 
emissions were calculated based on operations in branches and buildings 
where Swedbank has operational control.
• Scope 3 covers all indirect emissions, such as business travel, security trans -
port services, paper consumption, water consumption, waste and emissions from the manufacturing of employees’ IT equipment, such as computers, mon-
itors, tablets and phones. Scope 3 also includes emissions from the lending 
portfolio and investments through Swedbank Robur Fonder.

title: Scope 1
heading: Scope 1
start_phrase: The calculations use emission factors from internationally recognised data- bases such as IPCC, AIB, BEIS and the UN.
summary:
- Describes Swedbank’s greenhouse gas accounting methodology for scopes 1–3 aligned with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, using the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline); access and quality control (data checks, certificates, calculations) provided by U&We.
- Quantifies all seven Kyoto greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, NF3, SF6, PFCs) in CO2e using appropriate GWPs.
- Scope 1: Direct emissions from stationary fuels, heating, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage; vehicles estimated via Group financial controls; refrigerants via operational controls (refrigerant type and mass).
- Scope 2: Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, district heating/cooling/steam; calculated both location-based (grid-average factors) and market-based (supplier-specific/contractual instruments). Contractual instruments (EACs, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights) covered 37% of 2024 consumption; U&We assessed quality criteria; residual mix used where instruments don’t qualify or aren’t used. Boundary is operations with operational control.
- Scope 2 data and factors: Robust activity data for main operations; electricity purchases reported separately from grid charges; smaller branches allocated by employees (FTE) and floor area (m2). Emission factors from IPCC, BEIS, AIB, CIBSE, UN, and suppliers’ EPDs/specific mixes. CH4 and N2O included. Biogenic emissions generally not separated for location-based and district heating; separated for Estonia’s electricity mix.
- Scope 3 (own operations): Activity-data-based calculations for business travel, security transports, paper, water, waste, and employees’ IT equipment; no spend-based calculations in 2024; emission factors from IPCC, BEIS, CIBSE, UN, and select suppliers; share of primary supplier data not quantifiable.
- Data gaps and allocations: Where activity data is missing (e.g., small branches), emissions allocated using average per FTE and per m2; vehicle fuel assumptions based on an “average vehicle.” Approach follows GHG Protocol and is justified by strong coverage in main operations.
- Financed emissions (lending portfolio): Internal tool based on PCAF Standard. Formula: Financed emissions = underlying emissions × attribution factor (bank’s financed share of company/asset value).
- 2024 portfolio methodology enhancements: Expanded coverage across the full lending portfolio where methods exist; improved methods for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clearer scopes, better data sources, handling area anomalies, clarified consolidated vs company-level rules).
- Asset- and company-level methods: Asset-based for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, Shipping; company-level “Business loans”; top-down country-level for Agriculture and for Swedish private individuals in Forestry.
- Removals and sequestration: No company-level emission removals included; sequestration applied for Swedish private forestry holdings.
- Comparability and restatements: Due to expanded scope and methodological improvements, 2024 results aren’t directly comparable with 2023; historical figures restated for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and for Steel and Power Generation sectors (covered by climate targets).
- Governance and assurance elements: U&We manages platform access, checks market-based certificates against quality criteria, and validates calculations to support tracking against Swedbank’s climate targets (referenced in section E1-4).

heading: Scope 2
start_phrase: When calculating location-based scope 2 emissions, Swedbank has robust reporting of activity data in respect of purchased electricity, district heating and district cooling for its main operations.
summary:
- Purpose and framework: Swedbank calculates its greenhouse gas emissions annually using the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline), with access and quality control by U&We. Calculations follow the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, cover all seven Kyoto gases using CO2e and GWP values, and underpin tracking of climate targets.

- Data sources and QA: Emission factors come from recognized databases (IPCC, AIB, BEIS, CIBSE, UN; supplier EPDs for market-based electricity). U&We assesses the quality of market-based contractual instruments. Where activity data is missing, assumptions (e.g., “average vehicle”) and allocation methods are used in line with the GHG Protocol.

- Scope 1 methodology: Direct emissions from stationary fuels, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage. Vehicle emissions estimated via financial controls; refrigerants calculated via operational controls (type and charge). For small branches, emissions allocated using employees (FTE) and office area (m2).

- Scope 2 methodology:
  - Coverage: Purchased electricity, district heating and cooling, and steam for sites under Swedbank’s operational control; electricity purchases (kWh) separated from grid charges.
  - Dual reporting: Location-based uses average grid factors; market-based uses supplier-specific/contract-based factors (EACs, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights).
  - Contractual instruments: Represented 37% of 2024 consumption; where instruments fail quality criteria or are absent, residual mix factors are used. Swedbank does not sell energy (0% sales of certificates).
  - Gases/biogenic treatment: CH4 and N2O included; biogenic CO2 generally not separated (except for Estonia’s electricity mix); district heating biogenic not separated.

- Scope 3 coverage:
  - Own operations: Indirect emissions from business travel, secure transport, paper, water, waste, and manufacturing of employee IT equipment. Calculated from activity data (e.g., weights, passenger-km, hotel nights); no spend-based methods used in 2024. Mix of database and supplier-specific factors; the share based on supplier primary data cannot be quantified.
  - Investments and lending: Scope 3 includes emissions from the lending portfolio and investments via Swedbank Robur Fonder.

- Financed emissions (lending portfolio) methodology:
  - Standard and formula: Internal tool aligned with PCAF; Financed emissions = Emissions × Attribution factor (bank’s financed share of company/asset value).
  - 2024 developments: Expanded coverage to the full portfolio where methods exist; improved methods for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clearer scopes, better data sources, anomaly handling for area data, clarified use of consolidated vs company-level data).
  - Method set: Asset-based methods for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, Shipping; company-level method for Business loans; top-down country-level method for Agriculture and Swedish private Forestry.

- Allocation approach for smaller units: Where activity data is lacking, emissions for smaller branches are allocated using FTEs and floor area, leveraging Group estimates per employee and per m2, justified by strong data coverage in main operations.

title: Scope 3 emissions from the lending portfolio - Introduction
heading: Scope 3 emissions from the lending portfolio
start_phrase: Swedbank has created an internal calculation tool based on the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) Standard to calculate financed emissions for its lending.
summary: Overview of Swedbank’s Scope 3 financed emissions methodology for the lending portfolio using an internal tool aligned to the PCAF Standard, with the core formula Financed emissions = Emissions × Attribution factor (emissions from the company/asset multiplied by the bank’s financed share). In 2024, coverage was significantly expanded to the full portfolio where methods exist, with improved methodologies for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clarified product/asset scopes, new data source, handling of real estate area anomalies) and clarified rules on consolidated vs company-level data. Asset-based methods were developed for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, and Shipping; a company-level method for Business loans; and a top-down country-level method for Agriculture and private individuals in Sweden’s Forestry sector (with sequestration applied there). Company-level emission removals are excluded. Due to scope and methodological changes, 2024 results are not directly comparable to 2023; historical figures are restated for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and for Steel and Power Generation sectors with climate targets.
text:
Scope 3 emissions from the lending portfolio
Swedbank has created an internal calculation tool based on the Partnership for 
Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) Standard to calculate financed emissions 
for its lending. PCAF is used for the lending portfolio to align with industry prac-
tise on methodologies and better assess the relevance for different parts of the 
portfolio. The calculations are based on the following formula:
Financed emissions = Emissions x Attribution factor
Emissions = The emissions from an underlying company or an asset
 Attribution factor = The bank’s financed portion of the total value of the 
 company or asset
In 2024, the bank significantly expanded its coverage of calculations and devel -
oped new methodologies to take account of the full lending portfolio, where 
applicable methods exist. The methodology for calculating financed emissions 
related to Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate was improved, including 
 clarified product and real estate asset scopes, along with enhancements of the 
underlying data quality, such as a new information source and handling of anom-alies for area data for real estate properties. In addition, the rules regarding the 
use of consolidated data versus company-level data have been clarified.
Overall, the bank has developed asset-based methods for Real Estate, Motor 
Vehicles, and Shipping, and a company-level calculation method defined as 
 Business loans. For financing related to Agriculture and private individuals 
involved in the Forestry sector in Sweden, a top-down country-level method has 
been defined.
The calculations do not include company-level emission removals. Emission 
sequestration is applied for private individuals involved in the Forestry sector in 
Sweden as described below in the relevant section.
As the scope of the calculation is significantly expanded, the figures are not 
directly comparable with those published in 2023. Due to the methodological 
improvements for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate, the historical figures 
are restated to facilitate comparisons. Also, for the Steel and Power Generation 
sectors, which are covered by climate targets, the historical values have been 
restated to facilitate  comparison.

title: Recalculation rules
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.1 Recalculation rules
start_phrase: Swedbank has defined recalculation rules that describes the nature of events that would trigger a recalculation of financed emissions for either the base-year and/or other years, as well as a significance threshold that would be a subject for restatement.
summary:
- Establishes Swedbank’s recalculation rules for financed emissions, detailing when historical data (base year and/or other years) must be restated: structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), methodology changes, improved emission factors/activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), material errors, and addition of new scope 3 categories. Restatements are required when impacts exceed 5% for any target-setting sector/portfolio; smaller changes may be restated to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: mortgages (private persons/tenant-owner associations for housing); commercial real estate (property management companies for revenue-generating properties).
  - Scope: PCAF scope 1 and 2.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × building emissions.
    - Attribution factor: loan-to-value based on baseline market value; for loans originated after 2019, origination value is used.
    - Building emissions: annual kgCO2e from energy use. Sweden uses EPC energy consumption, heated area, heating source, energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates. Baltics use heated area, EPC, and PCAF EPC/building-type estimates; expired EPCs (up to 10 years) may be used. If data are missing, apply estimated heated area and PCAF building-type averages.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: PCAF scope 1 and 2; includes passenger cars, vans, motorcycles, heavy trucks; excludes tractors.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × vehicle emissions.
    - Attribution factor: financing amount divided by market value at origination.
    - Emissions: annual tailpipe or electricity-related emissions; prefer vehicle-specific tailpipe intensity (g/km) × annual distance. If unavailable, use PCAF estimates (make/model/type/fuel). Scope 2 electricity data from PCAF; annual distance inferred from PCAF when missing.

- Shipping:
  - Scope: loans secured by vessels; limited to ships >5,000 GT due to IMO reporting; covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × vessel emissions.
    - Attribution factor: financing divided by vessel market value at origination.
    - Emissions: annual tCO2e from fuel consumption using fuel- and engine/vessel-type-specific emission factors (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and Forestry:
  - Rationale: business loan approach overestimates for these segments; apply top-down method using National Inventory Reports.
  - Scope: agriculture (dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crops, other agriculture); forestry limited to private persons in Sweden (other forestry uses business loan method).
  - Method:
    - Agriculture: country territorial emissions (scope 1: on-farm and soils; scope 2: energy for machinery) plus limited scope 3 from mineral fertilizer production in core markets.
    - Forestry: includes CO2 sequestration; allocates based on private ownership share.
    - Allocation to Swedbank customers via market share and attribution factor.

- Business Loans (all other corporate lending not covered above):
  - Scope: PCAF scope 1, 2, and 3 (noting incomplete scope 3; PCAF proxies cover upstream only).
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × company emissions.
    - Attribution factor: Swedbank loan amount divided by company total assets (company or consolidated level aligned to emissions boundary).
    - Emissions data: customer-reported/public data where available; otherwise PCAF region/industry proxies; in some cases based on physical activity metrics (e.g., MWh). Use latest full-year data not older than 24 months.
text:
Recalculation rules 
Swedbank has defined recalculation rules that describes the nature of events 
that would trigger a recalculation of financed emissions for either the base-year 
and/or other years, as well as a significance threshold that would be a subject for 
restatement. In line with the defined rules, Financed emissions shall be recalcu -
lated in case of:
• Structural changes within Swedbank Group such as acquisitions 
and  div estments.
• Significant changes in GHG emission estimation methodology.
• Improvements in the accuracy of emissions factors or activity data  
(e.g., new PCAF data estimates, more granular emission factor information 
per energy source).
• Discoveries of errors that are deemed material, individually or collectively.
• Additions of new scope 3 categories.
The climate target and financed emission base-year publicly disclosed data 
needs to be updated if the restatements of the historical data are significant and 
aligned with the principles above. The impact is considered significant if the 
effects upwards or downwards exceed 5 per cent of any sectors/ portfolios, for which climate targets are set.
The bank might choose to restate the base year and other publicly disclosed 
data for changes deemed less significant to ensure consistency, relevance, and 
comparability of the reported data over time.

title: Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate - Introduction
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.2 Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate
start_phrase: Mortgages are defined as loans to private persons or tenant owner associations for acquiring residential housing.
summary:
Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate 
Mortgages are defined as loans to private persons or tenant owner associations 
for acquiring residential housing. Commercial real estate comprises all loans to 
companies within the property management sector for acquiring properties for 
revenue-generating activities, such as retail, offices, industrial properties and 
multi-family housing. In accordance with the PCAF standard, the method covers

text:
Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate 
Mortgages are defined as loans to private persons or tenant owner associations 
for acquiring residential housing. Commercial real estate comprises all loans to 
companies within the property management sector for acquiring properties for 
revenue-generating activities, such as retail, offices, industrial properties and 
multi-family housing. In accordance with the PCAF standard, the method covers 
scope 1 and scope 2 emissions.

title: Calculation methodology
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.2.1 Calculation methodology
start_phrase: Calculations of financed emissions for real estate consist of two parts: the attribution factor and the building’s emissions.
summary:
- Recalculation and restatement policy: Swedbank defines when financed emissions must be recalculated for the base year and/or other years. Triggers include structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, improved emission factors or activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates, more granular energy-source factors), material errors, and additions of new scope 3 categories. Publicly disclosed base-year data and climate targets are updated when impacts exceed a 5% threshold for any targeted sector/portfolio; optional restatements may occur for smaller changes to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Standards and scopes: Calculations align with PCAF. Each asset class combines an attribution factor with asset/company emissions. Coverage varies by class: real estate and motor vehicles cover scopes 1–2; shipping covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3; agriculture covers scopes 1–2 plus limited scope 3 (fertiliser production); business loans cover scopes 1–3 with noted scope 3 data gaps (PCAF upstream only).

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: Mortgages to private persons/tenant-owner associations; CRE to property companies (retail, offices, industrial, multi-family).
  - Method: Attribution via loan-to-value fixed at baseline market value (and origination value for loans opened after 2019). Emissions are annual kgCO2e from building energy use.
  - Data: Sweden uses EPC data (heated area, energy use, heating source), energy-source emission factors, and occupant energy use estimates. Baltics use heated area, EPCs (including estimates and those expired up to 10 years), and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates. If data lacking, use estimated heated area and PCAF building-type factors.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: Passenger cars, light-duty vehicles, motorcycles, heavy trucks; tractors excluded for data limitations.
  - Method: Attribution = financing divided by vehicle market value at origination. Emissions = annual tailpipe or electricity-related emissions. Highest quality uses vehicle-specific tailpipe g/km and annual distance; otherwise PCAF estimates by make/model, vehicle/fuel type. Scope 2 and missing annual distance sourced/estimated from PCAF.

- Shipping:
  - Scope: Loans secured by vessels; constrained by IMO reporting (ships >5,000 GT). Covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3 of vessels.
  - Method: Attribution = financing divided by vessel market value at origination. Emissions from annual fuel consumption and fuel-specific emission factors, reflecting engine type, vessel size/type, and fuel (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and Forestry:
  - Scope: Agriculture includes dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crop growing, other agriculture. Forestry applies to activities related to forestry for private persons in Sweden; other forestry activities use the business loan method.
  - Method: Top-down using National Inventory Reports. Agriculture covers scope 1 (operations, cropland/grassland organic soils) and scope 2 (energy), plus scope 3 limited to mineral fertiliser production. Forestry uses national data on CO2 sequestration with an assumption on private ownership share. Allocation to Swedbank based on market share and attribution factors. Results for non-private forestry are included under the business loan method.

- Business Loans:
  - Scope: Default for all business loans not covered by other methods; covers scopes 1–3, with incomplete scope 3 as companies improve methodologies; PCAF estimates only address upstream emissions.
  - Method: Attribution = Swedbank loan amount divided by company total assets (company or consolidated, aligned with emissions boundary). Emissions data sourced from public/bilateral company reports or PCAF region/industry proxies; sometimes activity-based (e.g., MWh generated). Financial and GHG data use latest full-year figures, not older than 24 months.
text:
Calculation methodology 
Calculations of financed emissions for real estate consist of two parts: the 
 attribution factor and the building’s emissions.
The attribution factor is equal to the property’s loan-to-value ratio fixed at the 
baseline’s market value and for loans opened after 2019, the origination value.
The building’s emissions are expressed as the amount of kgCO2e per year that 
the building’s energy usage generates. The scope includes assets that are 
deemed to generate emissions. The methodology to calculate the building’s 
emissions depends on data availability. In Sweden, for the highest data quality 
calculations, information on heated area, energy consumption provided from the 
Energy Performance Certificate (EPC), heating source and an emissions factor 
for each type of energy as well as an estimate on occupant energy usage is used. 
While in the Baltics, information on heated area, the EPC and respective EPC and building type-specific PCAF estimate is used. For the Baltic calculations, esti -
mated EPCs are also used, including EPCs that expired up to ten years ago. The assumption is that expired EPCs are still representative and provide useful infor-
mation even after expiry date, as it is better to have some energy intensity figure 
than just property type average. When such data used in the calculations is lack-
ing or incomplete for both Sweden and the Baltics, estimated figures for heating 
area and estimates provided by PCAF based only on building type are used.

heading: 5.2.7.3.2.3 Motor Vehicles
start_phrase: Motor vehicles are defined as financing towards passenger cars, light-duty vehi - cles (vans), motorcycles and heavy trucks.

Motor Vehicles 
Motor vehicles are defined as financing towards passenger cars, light-duty vehi -
cles (vans), motorcycles and heavy trucks. Tractors are excluded from the scope due to lack of accurate data on which to base the calculations on. In accordance 
with the PCAF standard, the method covers scope 1 and scope 2 emissions of 
motor vehicles.

Motor Vehicles 
Motor vehicles are defined as financing towards passenger cars, light-duty vehi -
cles (vans), motorcycles and heavy trucks. Tractors are excluded from the scope due to lack of accurate data on which to base the calculations on. In accordance 
with the PCAF standard, the method covers scope 1 and scope 2 emissions of

title: Calculation methodology
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.3.1 Calculation methodology
start_phrase: The financed emissions of motor vehicle loans are calculated by multiplying an attribution factor by the emissions of the vehicle.
summary:
- Recalculation rules: Swedbank defines when to restate financed emissions for the base year and/or other years. Triggers include structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, improved emission factors or activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), material errors, and additions of new Scope 3 categories. Public climate targets and base-year data are updated when restatements change any targeted sector/portfolio by more than 5%. The bank may also restate for smaller changes to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate: Defines mortgages (private persons/tenant-owner associations) and commercial real estate (property management for income-generating assets). Uses PCAF, covering Scope 1 and 2. Method = attribution factor (loan-to-value fixed at baseline market value; for loans post-2019, at origination value) × building emissions. Building emissions derive from energy use (kgCO2e/year). Sweden: uses EPC data (heated area, energy consumption, heating source), energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates for highest quality. Baltics: uses heated area, EPC, and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates; expired EPCs (up to 10 years) may be used; if data lacking, apply building-type and area estimates from PCAF.

- Motor Vehicles: Covers passenger cars, light-duty vehicles, motorcycles, heavy trucks; excludes tractors due to data gaps. Uses PCAF, covering Scope 1 and 2. Method = attribution factor (financing/market value at origination) × vehicle emissions. Emissions per year from tailpipe or electricity use; highest quality uses vehicle-specific tailpipe intensity and annual distance. If unavailable, PCAF estimates by make/model/type/fuel; Scope 2 from PCAF in all cases; distance inferred from PCAF if missing.

- Shipping: Applies to loans secured by vessels; data limited to ships >5,000 GT per IMO reporting rules. Covers Scope 1 and upstream Scope 3. Method = attribution factor (financing/market value at origination) × vessel emissions. Emissions computed from annual fuel consumption volumes and fuel-specific emission factors reflecting engine, vessel size/type, and fuel (HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol, etc.).

- Agriculture and Forestry: Uses a top-down approach based on National Inventory Reports by country and sector, as the general business loan method would overestimate emissions for this segment. Agriculture scope includes dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crop growing, and other agriculture. Forestry scope covers activities for private persons in Sweden; other forestry activities use the business loan method. Agriculture includes Scope 1 and 2 territorial emissions (operations; cropland/grassland organic soils; energy for machinery) plus limited Scope 3 for mineral fertilizer production in core markets. Forestry accounts for CO2 sequestration and private ownership share. Allocation to Swedbank is by market share and attribution factors.

- Business Loans: Default method for all other business lending. Covers Scope 1, 2, and 3 of customers; Scope 3 remains incomplete as companies improve coverage; PCAF estimates cover upstream only. Method = attribution factor (Swedbank loan/total assets at company or consolidated level) × company emissions. Emissions sourced from customer public reports, bilateral disclosures, PCAF region/industry proxies, or activity-based estimates (e.g., MWh generated). Financial and GHG data use latest full-year figures not older than 24 months.

- Cross-cutting themes: Heavy reliance on PCAF standards and datasets; clear attribution-factor frameworks; differentiated data-quality tiers and fallback proxies when primary data is missing; sector-specific scope boundaries; and governance for restatements to ensure consistency, relevance, and comparability over time.
text:
Calculation methodology 
The financed emissions of motor vehicle loans are calculated by multiplying an 
attribution factor by the emissions of the vehicle.
The attribution factor is equal to the financing provided for each motor vehicle, 
divided by the market value of the vehicle at loan origination.
The vehicle’s emissions are expressed as the amount of emissions per year 
that the vehicle generates. The emissions are generated either as tailpipe emis-
sions or emissions associated with electricity consumption. For the highest data 
quality, vehicle tailpipe emission intensity per kilometre is used in combination with annual distance driven for the vehicle. In cases where the tailpipe emission 
data point is unavailable, the bank retrieves estimates from the PCAF database. 
These estimates are based on vehicle attributes such as vehicle make/model, 
vehicle type and fuel type. For scope 2 emissions the data is retrieved from PCAF in all cases. In cases when vehicle-specific annual distance is unavailable, the 
measure is implied from the PCAF database.

title: Shipping - Introduction
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.4 Shipping
start_phrase: The shipping calculation method pertains to loans with vessels collateral for companies operating in industries related to shipping.
summary:
Shipping

title: Calculation methodology
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.4.1 Calculation methodology
start_phrase: Calculations of financed emissions for vessels consist of two parts: the attribution factor and the vessel’s emissions.
summary:
- Recalculation rules for financed emissions:
  - Triggers for restating base-year and/or other years include group structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), major methodology changes, improved emission factors/activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), material errors, and additions of new Scope 3 categories.
  - Publicly disclosed climate targets and base-year data are updated when restatement impacts exceed 5% up or down for any targeted sector/portfolio; smaller changes may also be restated to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: mortgages (private persons/tenant associations for housing); commercial real estate (property management for revenue-generating assets).
  - Scope: PCAF Scope 1 and 2.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor (loan-to-value at baseline market value; origination value for loans after 2019) × building emissions (kgCO2e/year from energy use).
  - Data approach: Sweden uses EPC data (heated area, energy consumption, heating source, emission factors) plus occupant energy; Baltics use heated area, EPCs, and PCAF EPC/building-type estimates; expired EPCs (up to 10 years) may be used; if data missing, use PCAF building-type and area estimates.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: passenger cars, vans, motorcycles, heavy trucks (tractors excluded); PCAF Scope 1 and 2.
  - Method: attribution factor (financing/vehicle market value at origination) × annual vehicle emissions.
  - Emissions: tailpipe intensity per km × annual distance, or PCAF estimates by make/model/type/fuel when missing; Scope 2 (electricity) from PCAF; distance may be inferred from PCAF when unavailable.

- Shipping:
  - Applies to loans secured by vessels; constrained to ships >5,000 GT due to IMO reporting.
  - Scope: Scope 1 and upstream Scope 3.
  - Method: attribution factor (financing/market value at origination) × annual vessel emissions from fuel consumption × fuel-specific emission factors (accounting for engine, vessel type/size, and fuels like HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and forestry:
  - Uses a top-down approach based on national inventory (territorial) emissions by country/sector due to overestimation observed with the business loan method.
  - Scope: agriculture (dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crops, other); forestry limited to private persons in Sweden; other forestry activities use the business loan method.
  - Method: agriculture includes Scope 1 (operations, cropland/grassland organic soils) and Scope 2 (energy); adds Scope 3 for mineral fertilizer production in core markets. Forestry uses national data on CO2 sequestration with an assumption for private ownership share.
  - Allocation to Swedbank based on market share and attribution factors.

- Business loans:
  - Default method for all other business lending.
  - Scope: customer Scope 1, 2, and 3 (noting incomplete Scope 3 coverage; PCAF proxies cover only upstream).
  - Method: attribution factor = Swedbank loan amount/total assets (company or consolidated, aligned with emissions data boundary); emissions sourced from public/bilateral company data, PCAF region/industry proxies, or occasionally activity-based (e.g., MWh). Uses most recent full-year data not older than 24 months.
text:
Calculation methodology 
Calculations of financed emissions for vessels consist of two parts: the 
 attribution factor and the vessel’s emissions.
The attribution factor is equal to the financing provided for each vessel, 
divided by the market value of the vessel at loan origination.
Vessel emissions are expressed in tonnes of CO2e that a vessel’s fuel con-
sumption results in each year. Accurate vessel emission calculations are based 
on the fuel emission factor for each fuel type, and respective volume of fuel con-
sumed in a given year. The emission factor reflects a ship’s engine type, the size 
and type of vessel and differs between the various fuel types, such as heavy fuel 
oil, marine gas oil, liquefied natural gas, biofuel, methanol, etc.

title: Calculation methodology
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.5.1 Calculation methodology
start_phrase: For agriculture the top-down emission from the National Inventory Report for industry agriculture includes a country’s territorial emissions covering scope 1 and scope 2 emissions.
summary:
- Recalculation rules and restatement threshold:
  - Swedbank defines when financed emissions must be recalculated for the base year and/or other years: structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, improved emission factors/activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), discovery of material errors, and additions of new scope 3 categories.
  - Publicly disclosed climate targets and base-year data are updated if restatements change any targeted sector/portfolio by more than ±5%. The bank may also restate for smaller changes to maintain consistency, relevance, and comparability.

- Portfolio coverage and methodological framework:
  - Methods align with the PCAF standard.
  - Calculations generally combine an attribution factor (exposure share) with asset- or company-level emissions, using the best available data and PCAF proxies where needed.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: mortgages to private persons/tenant-owner associations; commercial real estate loans to property management companies (retail, office, industrial, multi-family).
  - Scope: 1 and 2 emissions.
  - Attribution factor: loan-to-value based on baseline market value (and origination value for loans opened after 2019).
  - Emissions: annual kgCO2e from building energy use. Sweden uses EPC data, heated area, heating source, energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates; Baltics use heated area, EPC, and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates. Expired EPCs (up to 10 years) may be used; if data are missing, PCAF building-type estimates and area estimates are applied.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: passenger cars, light-duty vehicles, motorcycles, heavy trucks; tractors excluded. Covers scope 1 and 2.
  - Attribution factor: financing divided by market value at origination.
  - Emissions: annual tailpipe or electricity-related emissions. Prefer vehicle-specific tailpipe intensity and annual distance; otherwise use PCAF estimates by make/model, type, fuel. Scope 2 and missing distance values are taken/derived from PCAF.

- Shipping:
  - Applies to loans secured by vessels; data limited to ships ≥5,000 GT under IMO reporting. Covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3.
  - Attribution factor: financing divided by vessel market value at origination.
  - Emissions: annual CO2e from fuel consumption using fuel- and engine-specific factors (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and forestry:
  - Top-down approach using National Inventory Reports by country/sector due to limitations of the business loan method (noted as overestimating vs peers/statistics).
  - Agriculture scope: 1 and 2 territorial emissions (operations; cropland/grassland organic soils) plus scope 3 from mineral fertilizer production in core markets.
  - Forestry scope: applies to private persons in Sweden; uses CO2 sequestration data with assumed private ownership share; other forestry activities use the business loan method.
  - Allocation to Swedbank customers based on market share and attribution factor.

- Business loans (default method):
  - Applies to all other business lending. Covers scopes 1, 2, and 3, acknowledging incomplete scope 3 coverage; PCAF estimates cover upstream only.
  - Attribution factor: Swedbank loan amount divided by company total assets (company or consolidated level aligned with emissions data used).
  - Emissions data sources: customer public reports, bilateral disclosures, PCAF regional/industry proxies, and in some cases physical activity metrics (e.g., MWh). Financial and emissions data must be the latest full-year available and not older than 24 months.
text:
Calculation methodology 
For agriculture the top-down emission from the National Inventory Report for 
 industry agriculture includes a country’s territorial emissions covering scope 1 
and scope 2 emissions. Scope 1 includes GHG emissions from agriculture opera-
tions and GHG emissions from cropland and grassland organic soils. Scope 2 
GHG emissions come from the energy used for stationary and non-stationary 
machines. Scope 3 is added on top from other sources and includes only 
 emissions associated with production of mineral fertilisers used by agriculture 
industry in the core markets for the bank.
For forestry the top-down emission from the National Inventory Report for 
industry forestry includes the data on CO2 sequestration from forests and uses 
an assumption of share of ownership of the forest by private persons.
The allocation of emissions relating to Swedbank customers is carried out 
by market share and attribution factor information.

title: Calculation methodology
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.6.1 Calculation methodology
start_phrase: Calculations of financed emissions for business loans consist of two parts: the attribution factor and the company’s emissions.
summary:
- Recalculation rules and restatements:
  - Financed emissions are restated when there are structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, better emission factors/activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), material errors, or additions of new scope 3 categories.
  - Publicly disclosed base-year and climate target data are updated if impacts exceed ±5% for any targeted sector/portfolio; the bank may also restate smaller changes for consistency and comparability.

- Common calculation structure:
  - Financed emissions generally equal an attribution factor multiplied by asset/company emissions.
  - PCAF standards and datasets are the primary framework across asset classes.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: mortgages to private persons/tenant-owner associations; commercial real estate to property management companies (retail, office, industrial, multi-family).
  - Scope: 1 and 2.
  - Attribution: loan-to-value fixed at baseline market value (or origination value for loans opened after 2019).
  - Emissions: building energy use (kgCO2e/year). Sweden uses EPC energy consumption, heated area, heating source, energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates. Baltics use heated area, EPC, and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates; expired EPCs up to 10 years may be used; if data is lacking, use estimated heated area and PCAF building-type averages.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: 1 and 2; tractors excluded due to data gaps.
  - Attribution: financing amount divided by vehicle market value at origination.
  - Emissions: tailpipe or electricity-related. Prefer vehicle-specific g/km and annual km; otherwise use PCAF estimates (make/model/type/fuel). Scope 2 and missing annual distance are sourced/imputed from PCAF.

- Shipping:
  - Scope: 1 and upstream scope 3; constrained by IMO data availability (typically ships >5,000 GT).
  - Attribution: financing divided by vessel market value at origination.
  - Emissions: annual CO2e from fuel consumption volumes and fuel-specific factors reflecting engine type, vessel size/type, and fuel (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and Forestry:
  - Approach: top-down using National Inventory Reports (NIR) due to business-loan method overestimation evidenced by peers, country stats, and farm-level insights.
  - Agriculture scope: 1 (operations, cropland/grassland organic soils), 2 (energy), plus limited scope 3 for mineral fertilizer production in core markets.
  - Forestry: uses NIR CO2 sequestration data and an assumed private-person ownership share; applies only to private persons in Sweden; other forestry activities use the business loan method.
  - Allocation to Swedbank: market share and attribution factor.

- Business Loans:
  - Applies to all other business lending not covered by specific methods.
  - Scope: 1, 2, and 3; scope 3 remains incomplete; PCAF estimates cover upstream only.
  - Attribution: company loan amount divided by total assets (company or consolidated, aligned to emission data used).
  - Emissions data: customer public reports, bilateral data, or PCAF region/industry proxies; occasionally physical activity (e.g., MWh). Latest full-year data not older than 24 months.
text:
Calculation methodology 
Calculations of financed emissions for business loans consist of two parts: 
the attribution factor and the company’s emissions.
Attribution factor is the company’s loan amount within Swedbank divided by 
the companies’ total assets (as a proxy for total debt + equity). The company  -
level or consolidated asset value is used depending on the emission information used.
Customer emissions data is either taken from a customer’s public reports or 
provided by the customer on bilateral basis or estimated based on region-spe -
cific and industry-level proxy information provided through PCAF. In a few cases the emission data is estimated based on physical activity value (e.g., megawatt 
hours generated). The customer’s reported figures, both financial and related to 
GHG emissions, are based on the latest available full-year data, where the latest available data is not older than 24 months.

title: Deviations from PCAF
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.7 Deviations from PCAF
start_phrase: The bank has opted for certain deviations from the PCAF standard based on availability or quality of data.
summary:
- Overview of deviations from PCAF: Swedbank departs from PCAF where data availability/quality is limited, using alternative methods and certain assumption changes.
- Sector-specific methods:
  - Shipping: Uses vessel-level annual data aligned with International Maritime Organization requirements.
  - Agriculture and private forestry in Sweden: Applies top-down estimates using National Inventory Reports, market share, and financing data.
  - Swedish real estate (TOAs and assets with EPCs): Follows Swedish Bankers Association guidance, but uses European Environment Agency electricity emission factors instead of IEA; plans full alignment next year. TOA calculations designed to avoid double counting.
- Assumption deviations:
  - Business loans: Uses company asset value as a proxy for equity and debt in attribution factors due to internal data gaps.
  - Commercial real estate: No updated property valuations upon loan modification owing to system limitations.
  - Motor vehicles: Treats leasing contracts the same as lending per PCAF motor vehicle method.
- Next steps: Ongoing enhancement of financed-emissions methodologies, data quality, and transparency; plans to expand scope 3 category 15 to include facilitated emissions.
- Investments (Swedbank Robur Fonder):
  - Covered under GHG Protocol scope 3 category 15; uses TCFD-aligned WACI; not a PCAF signatory but adopts PCAF equations for financed emissions.
  - Applies to equities and corporate bonds using provider-sourced reported/estimated data.
  - Includes scopes 1 and 2; excludes scope 3 due to low reliability and volatility; cannot quantify the proportion of reported vs estimated data.
  - WACI: Holding carbon intensity × portfolio weight, summed; normalization redistributes weights when data is missing.
  - Financed emissions: Emissions × financed share, where financed share = investment holding / EVIC; summed at portfolio level.
  - Missing data assumptions: Assigns sector or global averages derived from the fund’s portfolio.
- Total GHG emissions and targets (CSRD E1-6):
  - 2024 used as baseline for first CSRD report; other climate targets have 2019/2022 baselines.
  - Lending portfolio targets are sectoral; investment targets are intensity-based; own-operations targets are absolute and not category-specific; no emission-category targets presented; potential future refinement; metrics not externally validated.
- Emissions inventory and materiality:
  - Longstanding own-operations emissions reporting, with ongoing expansion (e.g., review of Purchased goods and services and supplier materiality).
  - Financed emissions calculated for lending and investments to inform transition planning; methodological details provided elsewhere in the report.
  - Materiality assessment finds over 99% of scope 3 emissions stem from customers’ operations and fund investments (category 15); remaining categories (1–14) are immaterial for external reporting but continue to be monitored internally.
text:
Deviations from PCAF 
The bank has opted for certain deviations from the PCAF standard based on 
availability or quality of data. The deviations are related to methods as such or 
deviation from PCAF on certain assumption.
The bank has opted for own methods for shipping vessels, agriculture indus -
try, and real estate in Sweden for Tenant Owner Associations (TOA) and assets 
with available EPCs. Method applied to shipping vessels follows the vessel level 
annual data required by International Maritime Organization. Method applied for 
agriculture and private individuals involved in the forestry sector in Sweden fol -
lows top-down estimates using the relevant country National Inventory Reports, 
market share and financing information. Method applied to real estate in Sweden 
for TOAs and assets with available EPCs follows the guidance developed by 
Swedish Bankers Association, with an exception in the use of emission factors 
for electricity. Swedbank use European Energy Agency instead of International 
Energy Agency. The plan is to fully align with the method during next year. The 
 calculation for TOA is developed to avoid double counting.
The main deviation on certain assumptions include:
• For method business loans the bank uses company asset value for the calcu-
lation of attribution factor as a proxy for a company’s equity and debt value 
due to the lack of available data internally.
• When a Commercial Real Estate loan is modified currently no new property 
value is obtained due to current limitation of the internal data management 
systems. 
• For motor vehicle method the bank treats leasing contract the same way as 
lending described in PCAF method for motor vehicles.

title: Next steps
heading: 5.2.7.3.2.8 Next steps
start_phrase: Swedbank continues to develop its calculations and reporting of financed emissions, including by improving data quality and methodological aspects.
summary:
- Overview of Swedbank’s deviations from the PCAF standard driven by data availability/quality, including custom methods and assumption changes.
- Sector-specific methodologies:
  - Shipping: vessel-level annual data aligned with IMO requirements.
  - Agriculture and private individuals in Sweden’s forestry sector: top-down estimates using National Inventory Reports, market share, and financing data.
  - Swedish real estate (TOAs and assets with EPCs): Swedish Bankers Association guidance with an interim deviation using European Environment Agency electricity emission factors instead of IEA; plan to fully align next year; TOA method designed to avoid double counting.
- Key methodological assumptions/deviations:
  - Business loans: use company asset value as a proxy for equity and debt to compute attribution due to limited internal data.
  - Commercial real estate: no updated property value on loan modification owing to data system constraints.
  - Motor vehicles: leasing treated the same as lending under PCAF’s motor vehicle method.
- Next steps: ongoing enhancement of financed emissions calculations, data quality, and methodology; commitment to transparency; expansion of scope 3 category 15 to include facilitated emissions and improve data quality.
- Investments via Swedbank Robur Fonder (scope 3 category 15):
  - Method aligned with TCFD for weighted average carbon intensity (WACI); not a PCAF signatory but uses PCAF equations for financed emissions.
  - Coverage: equities and corporate bonds; emissions data (scope 1 and 2) from an external provider, using reported or modelled values; scope 3 excluded due to low reliability/volatility; share of reported vs estimated data not quantified.
  - Calculations:
    - WACI: holding carbon intensity multiplied by portfolio weight; normalize by redistributing weights when data is missing.
    - Financed emissions: emissions multiplied by financed share, where financed share = investment holding / EVIC; aggregated to portfolio.
  - Assumptions: where no data, apply sector or global averages derived from the portfolio.
- Total GHG emissions reporting (CSRD E1-6):
  - 2024 used as the baseline year for the first CSRD report; other climate targets use 2019 and 2022 baselines.
  - Targets: lending portfolio (sector-based), investments (intensity-based), own operations (absolute); not broken down by emission category; potential future categorization under evaluation; metrics not externally validated.
- Emissions inventory and scope:
  - Long-standing own-operations reporting; ongoing expansion as data improves; active review of suppliers for category “Purchased goods and services.”
  - Financed emissions calculated for lending and investments; main emitting segments identified; methodological details referenced elsewhere in the report.
- Significance assessment of scope 3:
  - >99% of scope 3 emissions from customers’ operations and fund investments (category 15); remaining categories (1–14) deemed insignificant (<1%) and excluded from external scope 1–3 reporting, though internally monitored for planning and target tracking.
text:
Next steps
Swedbank continues to develop its calculations and reporting of financed 
 emissions, including by improving data quality and methodological aspects. 
Swedbank is committed to continue to provide transparency and comparability in this area by showing its calculation methodologies and computations.
Going forward, the aim is to expand the category 15 scope 3 emissions of the 
bank by developing a method for facilitated emissions and continue improving 
the data quality.

title: Calculations of financed and intensity-based emissions in investments - Introduction
heading: 5.2.7.3.3.1 Calculations of financed and intensity-based emissions in investments
start_phrase: Swedbank Robur Fonder are covered by the GHG protocol, scope 3 category 15 (investments).
summary: This section outlines Swedbank Robur Fonder’s methodology for calculating financed and intensity-based emissions for equities and corporate bonds under GHG Protocol scope 3 category 15 (investments). Weighted Average Carbon Intensity (WACI, tCO2e/USDm revenue) follows TCFD recommendations, while financed emissions leverage parts of PCAF’s methods (e.g., equations), though the firm has not signed PCAF. Carbon data for holdings (scopes 1 and 2 only) is sourced from Swedbank’s data provider using company-reported figures or provider estimates; emissions are expressed for the reporting year either normalized by investee revenue or as absolute values, using the most recent available data. Scope 3 emissions are excluded due to low reliability and high volatility, and the share of reported versus estimated data cannot be quantified.
text:
Calculations of financed and intensity-based emissions in investments
Swedbank Robur Fonder are covered by the GHG protocol, scope 3 category 15 
(investments). The fund company’s method for calculating weighted average 
carbon intensity follows recommendations from the Taskforce on Climate-  
Related Disclosure (TCFDs). Swedbank Robur Fonder has not signed PCAF but has used parts of PCAF’s method in its development for calculating financed 
emissions, such as equations for financed emissions. The descriptions below 
apply to equities and corporate bonds. 
Carbon dioxide data for underlying investments is obtained from Swedbank’s 
data provider, which in turn obtains reported data from the companies or esti -
mates the data using its own estimation model. It expresses the emissions of each investment for the reporting year, either normalised with the investment’s revenue or without. The calculations include the fund holdings’ emissions scope 
1 and 2, and the most recently available carbon data is used. The fund holdings’ 
scope 3 emissions are not included due to low reliability and high year-to-year 
 volatility of these figures. Swedbank Robur Fonder cannot quantify the share 
which is based on reported data.

title: Weighted average carbon intensity (tCO2e/USDm income)
heading: 5.2.7.3.3.1.1 Weighted average carbon intensity (tCO2e/USDm income)
start_phrase: The carbon intensity of the underlying holding is multiplied by the investment’s weight in the fund.
summary:
- Explains Swedbank’s deviations from PCAF due to data availability/quality, including use of bespoke methods for:
  - Shipping: vessel-level annual data per IMO.
  - Agriculture and Swedish private forestry: top-down estimates using National Inventory Reports, market share, and financing data.
  - Swedish real estate (Tenant-Owner Associations and assets with EPCs): Swedish Bankers Association guidance with an interim exception using European Energy Agency electricity emission factors instead of IEA; full alignment planned next year. TOA method avoids double counting.
- Notes additional methodological assumptions/deviations:
  - Business loans: uses company asset value as a proxy for equity and debt to calculate attribution factors.
  - Commercial Real Estate: no updated property value upon loan modification due to internal data system limits.
  - Motor vehicles: leasing contracts treated the same as lending per PCAF motor vehicle method.
- Outlines next steps: ongoing enhancement of financed-emissions calculation and reporting, data quality and methodology improvements, increased transparency, development of a method for facilitated emissions to expand scope 3 category 15, and continued data quality upgrades.
- Describes scope 3 investments via Swedbank Robur Fonder:
  - Covered under GHG Protocol scope 3 category 15 (investments).
  - Uses TCFD-recommended weighted average carbon intensity (WACI); not a PCAF signatory but applies PCAF elements (e.g., financed-emissions equations).
  - Data from a provider using reported company data or modelled estimates; uses latest scope 1 and 2 only; scope 3 excluded for low reliability/volatility; share of reported vs estimated data not quantifiable.
  - WACI: holding carbon intensity × portfolio weight, summed; missing data leads to normalization (redistribution of weights).
  - Financed emissions: emissions × financed share; financed share = investment holding / EVIC; portfolio results aggregated.
  - For missing coverage, applies sector or global averages derived from the portfolio.
- Provides emissions reporting context (E1-6):
  - First CSRD-aligned report uses 2024 as baseline; other climate targets use 2019/2022 baselines.
  - Lending portfolio targets set by sector; investment targets intensity-based; own-operations targets absolute; no targets by emission category; future feasibility assessment planned; metrics not externally validated.
- Summarizes emissions inventory and materiality:
  - Longstanding own-operations reporting with continual expansion as data improves; active review of suppliers under Purchased Goods and Services.
  - Financed emissions calculated for lending and investments to inform transition planning and target-setting.
  - Materiality assessment shows >99% of scope 3 arises from customers’ operations and fund investments (category 15); remaining categories (1–14) are <1% and excluded from external scope 1–3 reporting, though own-operations scope 3 is still tracked internally.
text:
The carbon intensity of the underlying holding is multiplied by the investment’s 
weight in the fund. The result is then summarised at portfolio level.
If the data provider has no coverage for a holding, it is removed from the calcu-
lation and its weight in the portfolio is redistributed to holdings with data; this is known as normalisation.

title: Financed emissions (tCO2e)
heading: 5.2.7.3.3.1.2 Financed emissions (tCO2e)
start_phrase: The emissions of an underlying investment are multiplied by the financed share, where the financed share is calculated as:
summary:
- Explains Swedbank’s deviations from the PCAF standard due to data availability/quality, including use of bespoke methods for certain sectors.
- Custom methodologies:
  - Shipping: vessel-level annual data aligned with IMO requirements.
  - Agriculture and Swedish private forestry: top-down estimates using National Inventory Reports, market share, and financing data.
  - Swedish real estate (Tenant Owner Associations and assets with EPCs): Swedish Bankers Association guidance; uses European Environment Agency electricity emission factors instead of IEA; aims to fully align next year; TOA method avoids double counting.
- Key assumption deviations:
  - Business loans: uses company asset value as a proxy for equity plus debt to calculate attribution factors.
  - Commercial real estate: no updated property value upon loan modification due to data system limitations.
  - Motor vehicles: leasing treated the same as lending per PCAF motor vehicle method.
- Next steps: continue improving financed-emissions calculations and data quality; maintain transparency; expand Scope 3 category 15 to include facilitated emissions.
- Investments (Swedbank Robur Fonder):
  - Covered under GHG Protocol Scope 3 category 15; WACI method follows TCFD.
  - Not a PCAF signatory but uses PCAF elements (e.g., financed-emission equations).
  - Emissions data sourced via a provider (reported or estimated); uses Scope 1 and 2 only; Scope 3 excluded due to low reliability/volatility; share of reported vs. estimated not quantified.
  - WACI computed by weighting holdings’ intensities and normalizing for missing data.
  - Financed emissions calculated using financed share = investment holding / EVIC; missing holdings assigned sector/global averages derived by the fund company.
- Total GHG emissions (E1–6) and targets:
  - First CSRD-aligned report uses 2024 as baseline; existing portfolio targets have 2019/2022 baselines.
  - Lending targets are sector-based; investment targets are intensity-based; own-operations targets are absolute; no category-level targets yet; metrics not externally validated.
- Emissions inventory and scope:
  - Ongoing enhancement of own-operations inventory, including review of Purchased goods and services.
  - Financed emissions calculated for lending and for investments via Swedbank Robur.
- Scope 3 materiality assessment:
  - >99% of Scope 3 emissions arise from customers’ operations and fund investments (category 15).
  - Remaining categories (1–14) deemed insignificant (<1%) and excluded from external Scope 1–3 reporting, though still monitored internally for planning and target tracking.
text:
The emissions of an underlying investment are multiplied by the financed share, 
where the financed share is calculated as:
Financed share = Investment holding /EVIC holding
The result is then summarised at portfolio level.

Emissions inventory
Swedbank has a long history of reporting emissions from its own operations. Ongoing development gives Swedbank an understanding of reporting and the 
possibility to include more items in line with increased and better data  a vailability. 
An inventory was carried out before the measurements were started, and it is 
evaluated continuously to identify further relevant emission sources. For  example,  
a review has been initiated of the suppliers and which goods and services are important, from the perspective of emissions, in the category Purchased goods 
and services. 
Swedbank has calculated financed emissions through the lending portfolio, 
which is a key element of climate reporting for financial institutions. In the 
 climate transition planning work and calculations of financed emissions and 
related targets, an analysis was conducted to identify the main emissions in the 
lending portfolio. Emissions for financed emissions through investments in 
Swedbank Robur’s fund management activities have also been calculated.

title: Significant and non-significant scope 3 emissions
heading: 5.2.8.3 Significant and non-significant scope 3 emissions
start_phrase: A comparison was performed of the calculated scope 3 emissions from the lend- ing portfolio, investments and own operations.
summary:
- Purpose and context: The excerpt explains Swedbank’s methodological choices and reporting for financed emissions, highlighting deviations from the PCAF standard due to data availability/quality, and outlines scope 1–3 inventories, portfolio methods, and next steps.

- Deviations from PCAF:
  - Sector-specific methods:
    - Shipping: Uses vessel-level annual data per International Maritime Organization requirements.
    - Agriculture and Swedish private forestry: Applies top-down estimates using Sweden’s National Inventory Reports, market share, and financing data.
    - Swedish real estate (Tenant Owner Associations and assets with EPCs): Follows Swedish Bankers Association guidance, except it uses European Environment Agency electricity emission factors instead of IEA; plans to fully align next year. TOA calculation is designed to avoid double counting.
  - Assumption-level deviations:
    - Business loans: Uses company asset value as a proxy for equity and debt to calculate the attribution factor due to internal data gaps.
    - Commercial real estate: No new property valuation upon loan modification because of current data management limitations.
    - Motor vehicles: Treats leasing contracts the same as lending, consistent with PCAF’s motor vehicle lending method.

- Next steps:
  - Ongoing improvements in data quality and methodology; commitment to transparency by disclosing methods and computations.
  - Expansion of scope 3 category 15 to include a method for facilitated emissions and continued data quality enhancements.

- Scope 3 emissions from investments (Swedbank Robur Fonder):
  - Covered under GHG Protocol scope 3 category 15 (investments).
  - Method:
    - Weighted Average Carbon Intensity (WACI) aligned with TCFD recommendations.
    - Not a PCAF signatory but uses PCAF equations for financed emissions.
    - Applies to equities and corporate bonds.
  - Data:
    - Emissions data (scope 1 and 2 only) sourced via a data provider; uses reported or modelled estimates; most recent data applied. Scope 3 of holdings excluded due to low reliability and volatility; the share of reported vs. estimated cannot be quantified.
    - WACI: Holding carbon intensity × portfolio weight; missing coverage leads to normalisation (redistributing weights to covered holdings).
    - Financed emissions: Holding emissions × financed share; financed share = investment holding / EVIC holding; aggregated to portfolio.
    - If coverage is missing, Swedbank Robur assigns sector or global averages based on its portfolio.

- Emissions inventory and materiality (CSRD-aligned baseline year 2024):
  - Targets: Lending portfolio targets are sector-based; investment targets are intensity-based; operational targets are absolute. Targets are not broken down by emission category and are not externally validated.
  - Inventory development: Continuous expansion as data improve, including a supplier review for Purchased goods and services.
  - Significance assessment: Over 99% of scope 3 emissions come from customers’ operations and investments (category 15). The remaining scope 3 categories (1–14) are considered insignificant for external reporting but are monitored internally.

- Quantitative highlights (baseline year 2024):
  - Scope 1: 853 tCO2e.
  - Scope 2: 9,500 tCO2e (location-based); 3,417 tCO2e (market-based).
  - Significant scope 3 (category 15): 10,249,459 tCO2e
    - Lending portfolio: 7,965,039 tCO2e.
    - Investments (Swedbank Robur Fonder, scopes 1–2 of holdings): 2,284,420 tCO2e.
  - Total GHG (scope 1, scope 2, and significant scope 3):
    - Location-based: 10,259,812 tCO2e.
    - Market-based: 10,253,729 tCO2e.
  - Gases included: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs.
  - Group GHG intensity per net revenue (first-time metric; baseline 2024): 0.00007 tCO2e/SEKm (both location- and market-based); net revenue 148,290 SEKm.

- Lending portfolio reporting and methodology:
  - Largest climate impact arises via customers (indirect/financed emissions).
  - Sectors disclosed: Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, Shipping, and Business Loans (with additional targeted sectors like Power generation, Oil & Gas, Steel included within Business Loans).
  - Data basis: 2024 exposure and gross carrying amount; 2023 company-reported emissions used for target outcomes due to 2024 data unavailability at reporting time.
  - Attribution factor: Uses both gross carrying amount and exposure (including off-balance). PCAF and Pillar 3 Template 1 reporting use gross carrying amount, while certain climate targets use both gross and off-balance exposure to reduce volatility from clients drawing/undrawing credit lines.
text:
Significant and non-significant scope 3 emissions 
A comparison was performed of the calculated scope 3 emissions from the lend-
ing portfolio, investments and own operations. From this comparison, Swedbank 
has established that the significant emissions (over 99 per cent of scope 3 
 emissions) originate from its customers’ operations and from investments in 
funds (category 15). 
In light of the above, Swedbank’s insignificant emissions (less than one per 
cent of scope 3 emissions) are assessed to fall within the remaining 14 catego-
ries of scope 3 emissions (categories 1–14). These are therefore excluded from 
reporting of Swedbank’s scope 1–3 emissions. However, Swedbank continues to 
calculate and monitor scope 3 emissions from its own operations for internal 
planning and climate target monitoring.

summary:
The excerpt outlines Swedbank’s 2024 baseline and methodology for greenhouse gas (GHG) reporting, intensity metrics, and financed emissions:

- Establishes 2024 as the Group-wide baseline year for interim targets and future tracking. Reports Scope 1 emissions at 853 tCO2e; Scope 2 at 9,500 tCO2e (location-based) and 3,417 tCO2e (market-based); and significant Scope 3 emissions primarily from Category 15 (Investments) totaling 10,249,459 tCO2e, of which 7,965,039 tCO2e relate to the lending portfolio and 2,284,420 tCO2e to Swedbank Robur Fonder. Total GHG emissions are 10,259,812 tCO2e (location-based) and 10,253,729 tCO2e (market-based).

- Emphasizes that Swedbank’s largest climate impact arises indirectly via customers (financed emissions). Provides a sectoral view for the lending portfolio: mortgages, commercial real estate, motor vehicles, shipping, and business loans (the latter includes sectors with climate targets beyond mortgages and commercial real estate). Sectors are defined per PCAF and may differ from other report definitions.

- Frames the content within the Annual and Sustainability Report 2024, signaling a retrospective view for interim targets (2025) and longer-term targets (2030–2050), with 2024 serving as the anchor baseline.

heading: 5.2.8.5 Lending portfolio
start_phrase: Swedbank has the greatest impact on climate through the Group’s customers.
summary: Introductory overview of Swedbank’s financed emissions from its lending portfolio, stating the bank’s largest climate impact is via customers’ indirect emissions and that tables present total financed emissions by sector: mortgages, commercial real estate, motor vehicles, shipping, and business loans (which include sectors with climate targets beyond mortgages and CRE). Sector definitions follow the PCAF method. Data are based on 2024 exposure and gross carrying amount at year-end with available company-reported data; however, 2023 financed emissions outcomes were used to report climate target outcomes due to unavailable 2024 company data. Attribution factors consider both gross carrying amount and exposure (including off-balance), a key distinction for Business loans. text:
Lending portfolio
Swedbank has the greatest impact on climate through the Group’s customers. 
These indirect emissions arise from customers’ operations and activities. Swed-
bank’s total financed emissions through the lending portfolio are presented in the 
tables below, broken down into the following sectors: mortgages, commercial 
real estate, motor vehicles, shipping and business loans. The sectors that have 
climate targets in addition to mortgages and commercial real estate are included 
in business loans. Please note that the sectors are defined according to the PCAF 
method and can thus be distinguished from definitions in other parts of the report. The purpose of the tables below is to explain Swedbank’s total financed 
emissions through the lending portfolio.
The data presented below includes data from 2024 based on exposure and 
gross carrying amount as of the end 2024 and available company-reported data. 
The actual outcome of financed emissions as of 2023 was used to report the out -
come of the climate targets, as company-reported data for 2024 was not avail -
able at the time of reporting.
In calculating the attribution factor across various methods, two types of lend -
ing amounts are considered: the gross carrying amount and exposure. The latter includes both the gross carrying amount and off-balance exposure. These dis-
tinctions are crucial for the method Business loans due to the significant differ-
ences between these amounts. The PCAF and Pillar 3 Template 1 financed emis-
sion reporting utilize the gross carrying amount. In contrast, climate targets for 
sectors such as Power generation, Oil & Gas, and Steel are based on both the gross carrying amount and off-balance exposure. This approach helps mitigate 
volatility arising from clients drawing or undrawing credit lines year-on-year.

- Purpose and scope: Discloses financed emissions for the lending portfolio by sector, presented two ways—based on gross carrying amount and on exposure (including off‑balance). Covers Scopes 1 & 2 and Scope 3 emissions, PCAF data quality scores, and the share of company/asset‑specific data. Includes 2023 comparatives for Scopes 1 & 2.

- Sector coverage: Mortgages, Commercial real estate, Motor vehicles, Shipping, and Business loans, plus “Other” and portfolio totals.

- Portfolio scale and emissions (2024):
  - Gross carrying amount: 1,752,686 SEKm (plus Other 53,278; total 1,805,964).
  - Exposure view: 2,032,958 SEKm (plus Other 83,054; total 2,116,012).
  - Financed emissions totals:
    - Scopes 1 & 2: 3,580,063 tCO2e (gross-based) and 5,827,427 tCO2e (exposure-based).
    - Scope 3: 4,384,976 tCO2e (gross-based) and 11,723,505 tCO2e (exposure-based).
  - Average PCAF data quality (1=high, 5=low): Scopes 1 & 2 around 3.8; Scope 3 around 4.2–4.3.
  - Share of company/asset‑specific data: ~46% (gross) and ~50% (exposure).

- Sector insights:
  - Business loans dominate financed emissions, especially Scope 3, and have lower data quality scores (≈4.2–4.3) with limited company‑specific data (≈10–16%).
  - Shipping has the highest data quality (PCAF 1.0) with 100% asset‑specific data and includes Scope 3 reporting.
  - Mortgages and Commercial real estate show mid‑range data quality (≈3.5) with around half asset‑specific data and modest year‑over‑year reductions in Scopes 1 & 2 emissions compared to 2023.
  - Motor vehicles reported Scopes 1 & 2 emissions with moderate data quality (~3.1–3.2).

- Mortgage deep dive (gross carrying amount basis):
  - Total mortgages: 1,127,056 SEKm; Scopes 1 & 2 emissions 495,927 tCO2e; financed area 53,560 thousand m2; physical emission intensity 9.26 kgCO2e/m2; PCAF quality 3.5; 49% asset‑specific data.
  - Sweden vs Baltics:
    - Sweden: lower intensity (3.20 kgCO2e/m2); higher asset‑specific data in multi‑family (82%) and tenant‑owner associations (96%); tenant‑owner associations show the lowest intensity (1.67).
    - Baltics: significantly higher intensities (~39–42 kgCO2e/m2) across sub‑segments; asset‑specific data ~40–44%.
  - Sub‑segment highlights (Sweden): multi‑family homes have lower intensity (2.61) than single‑family (3.50); tenant‑owner associations exhibit the best combination of low intensity and high data specificity.

- Methodology and notes:
  - PCAF data quality scoring: 1 (high) to 5 (low); averages are weighted by gross carrying amount or exposure.
  - Company/asset‑specific data definition: for business loans, PCAF scores 1–2 count as company‑specific; for other sectors, PCAF scores 1–3 count as asset‑specific for any scope.
  - Exposure figures include off‑balance exposures.
